It places a `check` clause, `cd <tree> && git apply --reverse --check <patch>`, the check the patch can answer alone. I checked that command in a scratch repo: exit 0 over a tree that holds the work, exit 1 over one that lacks it. (R2) drive_locked's set-aside branch now takes `--answer decline`: for a decision set aside because a task can run, answer_refusal is asked first and refuses before the pending decision is dropped, so a decline with no --reason leaves the decision there for a second try with words. tasks.description: Carried low findings P155-R7, P155-R8, P155-R67 and P155-R73 (docs/audit/phases/P155.json review.findings), plus one found outside any finding: a fix task for a test-strengthening finding is created tdd with expectRedFirst although the red cannot be proved when the fix is in the test file. tasks.description: Carried low findings P155-R26, P155-R32 and P155-R57 (docs/audit/phases/P155.json review.findings) are three instances of one class: a task's recorded tests.gate selects no suite that reads or runs the files the task changed (CHANGELOG/COMPATIBILITY edits graded by four suites that never open them; a verify.sh/gate-parity change graded by suites that never import it), so a passed gate run is no evidence for the change. The repair is one mechanism, not three answers: when a gate is declared or a task closes, the files the task declares (or changes) are compared with what the gate's selected suites reach, through the same reading the affected-test derivation uses, and a file no selected suite reaches is named (warning at scope time, the close records it). Past tasks' recorded gates are the record of what was run and are not rewritten; say so for each of the three findings. Answer each by id.
